title: Native rollout receipt
description: One receipt records one component's rollout to one pinned version through one host's real install/upstream path (not a synthetic fixture), tiered T0-T6. It is a sibling of adoption/host-receipt.schema.json (per-host lifecycle acceptance) and of the layer-verdict schema catalogs/landscape/*.json winners use (scripts/landscape.py's VERDICT_STATUSES etc.), not a replacement for either. tools/sota-convergence/record_native_rollout.py implements this schema's rules directly in stdlib Python (no external JSON Schema library, matching adoption/host-receipt.schema.json's own sibling scripts/host_receipts.py) and is kept in sync with it by tests/test_record_native_rollout.py. adoption/tools/ecosystem-switch's own receipt gate (switch.md: 'tiers T0,T2,T4 and T1 passed or declared unavailable') and record_native_rollout.py's native_proven qualification rule (switch.md: 'T2 real workload + T4 + T5 (+T6 for services)') are two independent consumers of the SAME receipt shape with two DIFFERENT tier requirements; neither implies the other. Tier meanings fixed by an actual consumer: T0 install/version presence; T1 a GPU- or model-loading-dependent check that may be legitimately declared unavailable per host; T2 a real workload, not a --version/--help probe (adoption/host_receipts.py's BARE_HELP_OR_VERSION distinction applies here too); T4 an independent rerun's agreement with the first result (see the sibling 'independent' object below); T6 a live-service-specific check (a systemd unit actually restarted and health-probed under the new root, matching adoption/tools/ecosystem-switch's unit-restart operation kind). T3 and T5 are reserved ordering slots with no fixed meaning yet -- a future qualify wave should give each a concrete, testable definition rather than this schema guessing one; record_native_rollout.py and this file both treat an unknown-meaning tier as ordinary structural data, never a reason to reject a receipt.

id.description: <component_id>--<version>--<rid>, e.g. qmd--2.8.4--rollout-20260925a; record_native_rollout.py does not enforce an exact pattern beyond non-empty, unlike adoption/host-receipt.schema.json's stricter id (this schema has no host_id/date segments to bind).

status.description: Overall receipt outcome. adoption/tools/ecosystem-switch's receipt gate requires exactly "passed" here before any tier is even inspected.

component_id.description: A manifests/stack.json components[].id or a catalogs/landscape/*.json layers[].winners[].component_id, as adoption/host-receipt.schema.json's own component_id field documents.

version.description: The clean upstream version (e.g. "0.50.0"), never a bootstrap-linux.sh --tools-suffix staging marker (e.g. "-r20260925") appended to it: record_native_rollout.py copies this value verbatim into a landscape winner's pin, which validate_pins_v2 parity and platform_status.py's host-receipt binding then read as the plain upstream version a live host's own --version reports. adoption/tools/ecosystem-switch's apply accepts this value for a staged root (tools/<id>-<version>-<suffix>) as long as it is a prefix of that root's own version segment; install.root (below), not this field, is what binds the receipt to that specific staged root.

ref.description: e.g. a gh attestation run id or a detached .sig path; required unless kind is "none".

upstream.description: Exactly one of tag or commit is required ("tag|commit"); both may be present.

root.description: The install root with the literal placeholder ${STACK_HOME} in place of any real host path (e.g. "${STACK_HOME}/tools/qmd-2.8.4"), so a receipt never carries a personal absolute path.

marker_sha256.description: sha256 of a stable file inside root that identifies this exact install (e.g. its own lockfile or a --version marker file).

argv.description: The literal install command, with every path already using ${STACK_HOME}.

private_env_names.description: Names only, never values, of any environment variable the install read (docs/secret-storage.md).

assertion.description: What this command's exit/output was checked against, in words (e.g. "exit 0 and stdout contains the pinned version").

unavailable_reason.description: Required exactly when result is "unavailable" (e.g. "no GPU on this host"); refused otherwise.

rerun_label.description: Free-text identifying the independent rerun (a different host, session identity, or time), or "not_rerun" text explaining why none exists yet.

loki.description: Optional Loki query refs or log line hashes corroborating the rerun; observability/README.md's local-only scope applies.

txn.description: adoption/tools/ecosystem-switch ledger txn id this receipt's rollout ran under, when the receipt documents an actual switch (not required for a receipt written before ecosystem-switch adopted the component).

switch.description: Present only when this receipt corroborates an actual ecosystem-switch apply; absent for a receipt recorded before the component was switch-adopted.

evidence_class_claimed.description: Matches scripts/landscape.py's WINNER_EVIDENCE_CLASSES. This is the receipt AUTHOR's claim; record_native_rollout.py independently derives whether the claim is actually justified (T2+T4+T5, +T6 for a service, all passed => native_proven) rather than trusting it, and refuses to write an unjustified claim onto a winner.

limitations.description: Matches adoption/host-receipt.schema.json's limitations field: always at least one, e.g. what this rollout does not establish.

retained_native_failures.description: May be empty (a clean rollout retains none), but the key itself is always present: a failed attempt is kept for transparency, never silently dropped from the receipt that superseded it.
